After 48 years of vassalage, Free Commonwealth of Siñmarca is formally annexed by Helukenese.

The Dorudopatna Succession War is known as the Great Reckoning among the Tewilo, and as the Plunder among the Shedisha.
Festival of Lamps: The longest night in Yemapura is spent by firelight in Yemapura, with stories and gifts.
Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Confederation of Malkkarg launches a determined invasion into Merchant League of Pregha, igniting the Hundred Days War of Pregha.
Beaten back from stubborn ramparts, the invasion stalls. The War of Shahgird concludes after 1 year as Hikhok & Lihapisuyu successfully preserve their independence.
Tokwoh of Hikhok wins the glory sought in the War of Shahgird.
Regi II of Nogofe turns from the old cause toward knowledge.
The bells of Nogofe toll for the passing of Opa the Devout Pumotepola (a wasting sickness). The youth Regi ascends the throne under a regency council.

Galled by heavy biomass tribute and distant decrees, the citizens of Kingatuwa cast out their clan wardens! Renouncing all allegiance to Lihapisuyu, Rapatewa proclaims the sovereign Grand Marshalate of Kingatuwa.

Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Syndicate of Lihapisuyu marches swiftly upon Grand Marshalate of Kingatuwa. The drums of the Border War of Kingatuwa echo across the provinces.

Galled by heavy biomass tribute and distant decrees, the citizens of Wenọ cast out their clan wardens! Renouncing all allegiance to Yidrir, Ola proclaims the sovereign Artificer Directorate of Dibane.
Ola is acclaimed ruler of Artificer Directorate of Dibane.
A rust-blight sweeps the gene-farms of Legineland; biomass runs short.
The lords of Legineland hoard grain and sell it dear; the council of Legineland grows richer as the villages empty.
Master Artificer Yechsepa of Lolchos achieves worldwide acclaim with their magnum opus: "The Pneumatic Archimedes Screw".

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Rising against tyranny and privilege, the populace of Helukenese storms the seat of government! With the former regime swept aside, Himruw proclaims the foundation of the Workers' Federation of Helukenese!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Bakrigh divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Lihapisuyu!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Assassins from Bowofe strike in the dead of night, slaying Tutebe in the court of Kobolalibela!
QUEST COMPLETED: Deliverance of the High Scholar in Szefru! Himruw successfully frees the captive, escorting them to safety and earning 100 Gold in grateful tribute!

Fires leap on rooftops of Gevgird for the new-year spring; Yidrir jumps the flames for luck.

A cold upwelling chills the domes of Bakrigh; kelp farms wither and the reefs bleach.

Vrivvo II of Dravvekot comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Solemn rites echo through Dravvekot following the death of Shrimvemra the Gentle Yvanrulvisri (poison). Vrivvo is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.

Chi'chuku is acclaimed ruler of United Provinces of Lukavo.
Nekise (Master Artificer) designs a rapid-firing ballista mechanism adopted by frontier garrisons in Yoniwowu.
Kikofe (Archmage) unravels a supernatural anomaly in the mountains in Wigogi.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Oyo-petege! Foso seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Artificer Directorate of Oyo-petege!
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Lukavo! Resha seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the High Realm of Lukavo!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Krapura stir mutiny among garrison troops in Gaseguno!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Vrabad stir mutiny among garrison troops in Ta'wi!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Ngussara embarks upon the Rescue of the Ice-Stranded Hunters near Ruviq! Ngussara learns that a hunting party has drifted out on a broken ice floe near Ruviq.

NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Goldzamin pave the Zhilkvazh-Pregrad Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Zhilkvazh and Pregrad (+trade, +stability).

Unrest of the year: tax riots in Zimdenstan (Kingatuwa); bread riots in Dravvekot.

Foso of Oyo-petege comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Foso of Oyo-petege fills the treasury, the wealth long sought.
Resha of Lukavo comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Desho of Hameva lets go of the aim for glory.
Chi'chuku of Lukavo fills the treasury, the wealth long sought.

In the lands Lenmennesnel won by the sword, 8 districts now speak the Chanmat tongue and keep its customs.
After years of agitation, temperance is enacted in Oyo-petege; Fome Lineno is cheered through the streets of Fugo.
Under the hand of Helukenese, Geshochu gives up gene castes for green commons.
The gene vats of Vrabad yield a bumper harvest: fat grain and fast-grown livestock swell its towns.
Delvers of Nogofe break into a vast geode cavern beyond Nogofe; the deep realm grows.
The tiny Republic of Panusi seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Ngogha.

A whirlwind walks across the plains of Krapura in high summer and through the heart of Tiwcocha, scattering roofs like leaves.
A mountainside gives way above Qihmarca; houses, a road and a mill are buried in a single roar of mud and stone.

monsters.name: The Eclipse Wolf
monsters.lore: A terrifying dread wolf of midnight taigas, capable of swallowing whole warbands beneath the winter moon.

monsters.name: Glacies the Glacial Drake
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: The Emerald Qilin
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: The Great Sun Lion
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: The Frost-Maned Guardian
monsters.lore: A colossal pale tiger of snow-clad ridges, silent as autumn wind, that warbands speak of only in whispers.

monsters.name: Abyssal Terror
monsters.lore: A colossal multi-tentacled sea monster capable of pulling entire armadas down into the black abyss.

monsters.name: The Storm Roc of the Badlands
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: Iron-Hide Boar
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: Bakunawa the Moon-Eater
monsters.lore: A great sea serpent that rises to swallow the moon; villagers drive it back by banging pots and pans until it spits the moon out.

monsters.name: Sasabonsam of the High Branches
monsters.lore: A long-legged forest being that dangles from the canopy to snatch the careless traveller.

monsters.name: The Simurgh of Mount Qaf
monsters.lore: A vast and wise bird that has seen the world destroyed three times; it may help a hero or test them.

monsters.name: Timingila the Whale-Swallower
monsters.lore: A sea monster of the old epics so vast it swallows whales whole, and is itself swallowed by something larger still.

wonders.name: The Sun City
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, The Sun City remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +50 Realm Treasury Gold and doubles local carrying capacity.

wonders.name: Academy of the Seven Mysteries
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, Academy of the Seven Mysteries remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +30 Innovation and regularly produces famous thinkers and inventors.

wonders.name: The Iron Spire
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, The Iron Spire remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +15 Martial to rulers and trains celebrated champion heroes.

wonders.name: Adamantine Foundry of the Deep
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, Adamantine Foundry of the Deep remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +20 Army Power and periodically bestows legendary weapons upon the realm.

wonders.name: Titan's Causeway
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, Titan's Causeway remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +25% Trade and caravan speed across frontier territories.

wonders.name: The First Timber
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, The First Timber remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +15 Realm Stability and fertility to surrounding provinces.

wonders.name: Drowned Palace of Pearls
wonders.lore: Erected in the mythic ages of Misuchu, Drowned Palace of Pearls remains one of the supreme wonders of the mortal world.
wonders.effect: +20 Intrigue and reveals sunken treasures of antiquity.

wonders.name: The Imperial Collegium
wonders.lore: Commissioned in year 2 by Bizhtira of Talshuz. Its soaring spires and monumental craftsmanship stand as a testament to mortal ambition.
wonders.effect: +30 Innovation and regularly produces famous thinkers and inventors.

wonders.name: Shrine of the Fallen Emerald Qilin
wonders.lore: Consecrated in year 6 by Nata to commemorate the historic victory over The Emerald Qilin. Pilgrims travel across provinces to touch the fabled bones and give praise.
wonders.effect: +20 Realm Stability and attracts pilgrims and valiant champions from foreign lands.

wonders.name: The Tower of Trials
wonders.lore: Commissioned in year 6 by Pawina of Sawamawuhu. Its soaring spires and monumental craftsmanship stand as a testament to mortal ambition.
wonders.effect: +15 Martial to rulers and trains celebrated champion heroes.

wonders.name: Tower of Starfall
wonders.lore: Commissioned in year 8 by Shabza of Pregha. Its soaring spires and monumental craftsmanship stand as a testament to mortal ambition.
wonders.effect: +25 Innovation and protection against supernatural disasters.

wonders.name: Shrine of the Fallen Golden Sun Lion

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards

people.name: Irijara
people.title: magician
people.look: A wiry figure with bright gold eyes, braided starlight hair and high pointed ears, and pierced ears hung with small river-pearls. Carries a rune-inscribed focus rod and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Pøla
people.title: hero
people.look: A broad-shouldered figure with deep violet eyes, braided beard hung with ancient bronze talismans, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a polished buckler and squints thoughtfully before every reply.

people.name: Ivijum
people.title: artist
people.look: A sinewy figure with hazel eyes, swept-back silver-blond tresses and long tapered ears, and stern, deeply etched brow lines. Carries charcoal-stained cuffs and a lute and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Rasa
people.title: Khagan of Rödokent
people.look: A stocky figure with deep violet eyes, desiccated royal wrappings and a gilded death-mask, and ritual ash-marks along the brow. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Shybkirsy
people.title: hero
people.look: A statuesque figure with deep violet eyes, pearlescent scales along the temples and webbed ears, and calloused hands stained with ink and oil. Carries a notched masterwork blade and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Yera
people.title: general of Semmfawy
people.look: A lithe figure with deep violet eyes, braided beard hung with ancient bronze talismans, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a wolf-pelisse clasp and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Thevy
people.title: hero
people.look: A wiry figure with dark obsidian eyes, frost-rimed braids and granite-carved features, and pierced ears hung with small river-pearls. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and squints thoughtfully before every reply.

people.name: Ingupanga
people.title: Angakkuq of Nupamoshu
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with pale ice-blue eyes, swept-back silver-blond tresses and long tapered ears, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Halrwidla
people.title: hero
people.look: A stocky figure with copper-flecked eyes, asymmetric crown-horns and warp-etched skin, and stern, deeply etched brow lines. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Dönö
people.title: prophet
people.look: A lithe figure with deep violet eyes, parchment skin, sunken sockets alight with cold blue fire, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries ash-streaked robes and a铜 bell and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Schulb
people.title: prophet
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with pale ice-blue eyes, iridescent gill-fins and coral-threaded hair, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries ash-streaked robes and a铜 bell and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Quku
people.title: prophet
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with storm-grey eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and ritual ash-marks along the brow. Carries a tablet of prophecies and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Cho'wi
people.title: hero
people.look: A stocky figure with sea-green eyes, a sharp grin and soot-smudged goggles on the forehead, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a polished buckler and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Dela
people.title: prophet
people.look: A lithe figure with bright gold eyes, braided beard hung with ancient bronze talismans, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Wih
people.title: prophet
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with storm-grey eyes, asymmetric crown-horns and warp-etched skin, and pierced ears hung with small river-pearls. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Sova
people.title: prophet

people.look: A wiry figure with hazel eyes, pearlescent scales along the temples and webbed ears, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Ingulavuva
people.title: prophet

people.name: Wiha
people.title: Ard Rí of Gotwy
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with copper-flecked eyes, asymmetric crown-horns and warp-etched skin, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.title: prophet

events.text: COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Shatuwi detonate powder stores in Sinisu, gutting frontline regiments!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Ngia are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Y'ragh!
QUEST COMPLETED: Recovery of the Crown Jewels in Zoda! Ihyixx unlocks the sealed adamantine vault, unearthing the sacred relic Ancient Spear of Vechoshe to global acclaim!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Wiha embarks upon the Expedition to the World Tree in Bukegagorod! Wiha outfits an intrepid party of scholars and veterans to map the perilous approaches to Bukegagorod.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Byrumoshu pave the Komov-Hyrypyku Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Komov and Hyrypyku (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Shatuwi pave the Futu-Rusituju Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Futu and Rusituju (+trade, +stability).
The Komov–Hyrypyku Tramway opens: the first bio-tram of Byrumoshu runs from Komov to Hyrypyku, with stations in both towns.

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Dar Yusa! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).
PATRON MIRACLE: Zephyros the Sky-Sovereign hurls deafening thunderbolts across the frontiers of Thothufjord, scattering hostile vanguards with righteous gales (+15% army power).
RUINOUS GIFT: Tzannik the Architect of Fate mutates the weave of fate in Mashice! Arcane mutations grant uncanny clairvoyance and secret gold, at the cost of civil panic (+30 gold, -6 stability).
The Children of the One Bloom spreads a whispering fungus through Wapmab, promising one shared mind for all.
The Children of the One Bloom spreads a whispering fungus through Qusiyya, promising one shared mind for all.

The War of Zhupa is known as the Vindication among the Tsogapa, and as the Aggression among the Pnamkochshovpptsa.
River Blessing Day: Bonfires on the hills of Chosizu greet the high sun above Wechigaqudu.
Harvest Home: Granaries of Kabov are opened at Kabov; the whole town eats until dusk.
Day of the Mummies: Families in Yamachi set out lamps and food for their dead at Piqasamarca.
Feast of the Ancestors: Families in Hvobry set out lamps and food for their dead at Hvobry.
Envoys from Vaviska and Mashomir exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Zhograd and Robogo exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Hvobry and Hvobry exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Semmfawy and Oghyth exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
With swords drawn and ancient pacts invoked, Merchant League of Vaviska marches against Grand Marshalate of Zose. The War of the Zose Crown begins.
The Zhograd–Latlul War reaches its conclusion after 4 years of bloodshed: Zhograd & Lufovi triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.

ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Dictated at swordpoint by Zhograd, the old institutions of Workers' Federation of Latlul are dismantled! The defeated realm is reorganized into the Grand Marshalate of Latlul under a new constitutional treaty.
Chisy II of Zhychice turns from the old cause toward glory.
In Zhychice, Shyhuga the Fearless Divepin departs this life, succumbing to a wasting sickness. The child Chisy (age 2) is crowned beneath a wary council of regents.
Shalatsa of Gofuzy comes to the throne bent on glory.
A perilous interregnum grips Gofuzy following the heirless death of Rohyda (old age). Retainers of House Galin storm the assembly and usurp the crown.
In the bustling market squares of Kesalo, the charismatic prophet Kysa begins preaching miraculous visions, winning throngs of converts to the newly revealed Kysaite Cult.
Upon the fertile crossroads of Lasakuwi, allied elders and chieftains swear a founding compact, raising the banners of the sovereign Principality of Lasakuwi.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Qawa storm the government palace in Vulaqiniq! The faction seizes control, establishing the Commercial Union of Vulaqiniq.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Chenkik detonate powder stores in Ngebri, gutting frontline regiments!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Gofuzy are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Ngia!
QUEST COMPLETED: Quest for the Sunken Heirloom in Dikigyka! Schulb unlocks the sealed adamantine vault, unearthing the sacred relic Hallowed Crown of Kivopushuzhe to global acclaim!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Ilxaq'loth pave the Ayghloth-Rujnguv Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Ayghloth and Rujnguv (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Beta Shuzilo pave the Shezitgondar-Dimishede Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Shezitgondar and Dimishede (+trade, +stability).
Deno, sprouting luminous lichen from their skin, preaches communion with the great mycelium in Socholöbulag.
Rogue splicer Lynuma cures a blight in Zunyhido that the clans of Gofuzy engineered; the poor make them a saint.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Rusituju (Vulaqiniq).

monsters.name: The Thousand-Tentacled Horror
monsters.lore: A colossal multi-tentacled sea monster capable of pulling entire armadas down into the black abyss.

monsters.name: Behemoth the Earth-Shaker
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: Snow-Ghost of the High Passes
monsters.lore: A colossal pale tiger of snow-clad ridges, silent as autumn wind, that warbands speak of only in whispers.

monsters.name: The Celestial Raptor
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: The Rime-Bane
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: Shadow of the Loch
monsters.lore: An elusive plesiosaur-like lake cryptid spoken of in local campfire folklore, surfacing only when mists veil the waters.

monsters.name: Fenrir Shadow-Stalker
monsters.lore: A terrifying dread wolf of midnight taigas, capable of swallowing whole warbands beneath the winter moon.

monsters.name: The Emerald Qilin
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: The Three-Headed Zmey
monsters.lore: A many-headed dragon of the steppe-forests that grows heads back as fast as heroes cut them.

monsters.name: The Qalupalik of the Ice Edge
monsters.lore: A sea creature with long nails that steals children who wander too close to the ice.

monsters.name: The Each-uisge of the Loch
monsters.lore: A water horse that lets riders mount, then plunges into the loch with them stuck fast.

monsters.name: Kappa of the Reed Pools
monsters.lore: A water imp with a dish of water on its head; bow to it, and courtesy forces it to bow back and spill its strength.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards

people.title: Oba of Nigisi
people.look: A wiry figure with bright gold eyes, glossy iridescent mandibles and compound facets, and ritual ash-marks along the brow. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Ayhahxa
people.title: Hierophant of Azhugg
people.look: A statuesque figure with pale ice-blue eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a signet ring of state and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Sofinu
people.title: hero
people.look: A sinewy figure with amber eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Uy'ehzayr
people.title: hero
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with amber eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and ritual ash-marks along the brow. Carries a notched masterwork blade and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Uqyutgha
people.title: Hierophant of Azhugg
people.look: A lithe figure with slate-grey eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Yhyu't
people.title: Hierophant of Azhugg
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with dark obsidian eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a signet ring of state and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Futi
people.title: Mansa of Kotate
people.look: A statuesque figure with bright gold eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Qi'erleoha
people.title: Hierophant of Zo'olgugg
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with amber eyes, parchment skin, sunken sockets alight with cold blue fire, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Rawora
people.title: Mansa of Kotate
people.look: A stocky figure with sea-green eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and calloused hands stained with ink and oil. Carries a signet ring of state and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Tido
people.title: Mansa of Kotate
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with pale ice-blue eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries a signet ring of state and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

The Great Death burns itself out at last; survivors in Muju bury the dead and open the shutters.
Envoys from Rokumako and Kotate exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.

Denouncing ancient covenants, the heralds of Free Trading Cities of Ruwomi proclaim war upon United Provinces of Yutetate. Trumpets sound across the frontier as the Yutetate Campaign begins. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Fudadida rally to Yutetate's side.
Denouncing ancient covenants, the heralds of Commune of Rokuso proclaim war upon Merchant League of Nomaba. Trumpets sound across the frontier as the Invasion of Nomaba begins.
The Bapo–Morenebaru War reaches its conclusion after 2 years of bloodshed: Bapo triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.
Exhausted by protracted attrition, both sides sign an armistice concluding the War of the Sobaland Crown (1 year). Scabbards are sheathed and the status quo ante is restored.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of the Pano Crown after 1 year. With frontiers redrawn, Qasr Fukwir dictate terms to the vanquished.
Ikaj of Umuj takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Solemn rites echo through Umuj following the death of Inaja the Younger Aquqap (a hunting accident). Ikaj is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.
To'ta II of Neta takes up the cause of the safety of the clan-state.
In the royal halls of Neta, Wa'pesa Silver-Tongue Ji'ekawuebe breathes their last, succumbing to poison. To'ta ascends the ancestral throne amid solemn acclamation.
Ngasara of Morenebaru takes up the cause of the spread of the faith.
A perilous interregnum grips Morenebaru following the heirless death of Yere (fever). Retainers of House Tebabebehe storm the assembly and usurp the crown.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Lepudugu take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Hutobayu, they hoist republican banners beneath Wela to establish the Free Commonwealth of Sumalamuge.
Wela is acclaimed ruler of Free Commonwealth of Sumalamuge.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Iron Dominion of Hutobayu marches swiftly upon Free Commonwealth of Sumalamuge. The drums of the Hundred Days War of Sumalamuge echo across the provinces.
Sedugö (Archmage) transmutes lead into silver, filling the state coffers in Süvu.
Mivi (Master Artisan) completes a cathedral ceiling fresco celebrating the history of the clan-state in Taloturoa.
Ronoko (Philosopher) calculates the true circumference of the world from tower shadows in Moromabougou.

After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Bunwir give way! Vanguard forces of Qasr Fukwir storm the royal seat of Bunwir, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
Gathering of the Clans: Warriors of Közusi parade and wrestle in the squares of Reqübulag to honour the old victories.
Banners trampled and throne abandoned, Cybernetic Union of Bunwir ceases to exist as a sovereign power. Wuytuzquqa Saqqut flees the ashes of their former dominion.
A victor's peace is forged: after 2 years of campaign in the Qasr Fukwir–Bunwir War, Qasr Fukwir & Neta & Hiwetlo prevail, annexing contested borderlands.

monsters.name: Snow-Ghost of the High Passes
monsters.lore: A colossal pale tiger of snow-clad ridges, silent as autumn wind, that warbands speak of only in whispers.

monsters.name: The Rime-Bane
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: Titan of the Steppes
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: Brimstone the Dragon-King
monsters.lore: An ancient volcanic dragon sleeping atop mountains of melted gold, reducing invading armies to calcined bones.

monsters.name: The Thousand-Tentacled Horror
monsters.lore: A colossal multi-tentacled sea monster capable of pulling entire armadas down into the black abyss.

monsters.name: The Celestial Raptor
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: Nessie the Mist-Lurker
monsters.lore: An elusive plesiosaur-like lake cryptid spoken of in local campfire folklore, surfacing only when mists veil the waters.

monsters.name: The Great Sun Lion
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: The Timingila of the Deep
monsters.lore: A sea monster of the old epics so vast it swallows whales whole, and is itself swallowed by something larger still.

monsters.name: The Ahuizotl of the Lake
monsters.lore: A water dog with a hand at the end of its tail that drags fishermen beneath the lake.

monsters.name: Sasabonsam of the High Branches
monsters.lore: A long-legged forest being that dangles from the canopy to snatch the careless traveller.

monsters.name: Tepegöz the One-Eyed
monsters.lore: A one-eyed giant of the steppe epics, slain only by a hero clever enough to blind him.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards
